statement: The province should reinstate and raise the consumer carbon tax to cut emissions, even if it increases the cost of fuel.
notes: NDP scrapped the consumer carbon tax in 2025; Greens want a rising carbon price; Conservatives and OneBC oppose any consumer carbon tax. Sharp three-way split that also separates the NDP from its 2024 base.

statement: The government should cut taxes for middle- and higher-income earners even if that means smaller public services.
notes: Defines the fiscal cleavage: Conservatives/OneBC sell tax relief as the core promise; NDP and CentreBC prioritise services; Greens refuse to trade services for cuts.

statement: The province should introduce a wealth tax on the highest earners to fund public services.
notes: NDP and Greens are open to higher taxes on top earners; Conservatives/OneBC oppose; CentreBC cautious. Tests the left flank against the centre-right.

statement: BC should balance its budget even in uncertain economic times, cutting spending to get there.
notes: The ballooning deficit is a top-3 issue for Conservative voters (44%) but near-irrelevant to NDP voters (7%). Conservatives/OneBC centre it; NDP argues invest-first; Greens prioritise climate spend.

statement: The government should cap the price of groceries and fuel to fight the rising cost of living.
notes: Populist cost-of-living lever. NDP and OneBC flirt with interventions; Conservatives prefer tax cuts and supply; Greens are sceptical price caps work.

statement: The minimum wage should rise automatically with inflation, even if it pressures small businesses.
notes: NDP/Greens support automatic indexation; Conservatives/OneBC warn of small-business costs; CentreBC is split.

statement: BC should reduce the deficit mainly by shrinking the size of the public service.
notes: Austerity signal separating Conservatives/OneBC from NDP/Greens; CentreBC sits in the middle. Sharper than q04 because it names the instrument.

statement: Help with the cost of living should go to low-income households through targeted rebates rather than broad tax cuts.
notes: Tests whether relief should be means-tested. NDP/Greens favour rebates; Conservatives/OneBC favour broad cuts.

statement: The province should raise taxes on large corporations to pay for public services.
notes: Classic left-right separator independent of the carbon-tax fight; NDP/Greens/BCE rise; Conservatives/OneBC oppose.

statement: The province should override municipal zoning rules to force more density near transit stations.
notes: NDP's signature housing intervention; Conservatives and property-rights voices push back; CentreBC is sympathetic; Greens supportive. Tests provincial power over local planning.

statement: Rent controls should be strengthened and extended to more units.
notes: NDP/Greens favour; Conservatives/OneBC say rent controls suppress new supply; CentreBC cautious.

statement: The government should build and own affordable rental housing itself, rather than relying on the private market.
notes: Distinguishes state-builds from market-builds. NDP/Greens/BCE support public build; Conservatives/OneBC prefer private developers.

statement: BC should tax vacant and speculator-owned homes more heavily.
notes: NDP already levies speculation taxes; Greens want more; Conservatives/OneBC would cut them. Tests redistribution against property rights.

statement: Homeowners should be protected from policies that reduce the value of their property.
notes: Frames NDP densification as a threat to existing owners. Conservatives/OneBC lean in; NDP/Greens reject the premise.

statement: Municipalities, not the province, should have the final say over housing density in their neighbourhoods.
notes: Local-control vs provincial-override. Conservatives/OneBC champion municipalities; NDP defends its overrides; Greens split.

statement: Short-term rentals such as Airbnb should be tightly restricted to free up homes for residents.
notes: NDP has restricted them; Greens support; Conservatives/OneBC want owners to keep flexibility. High salience in tourist communities.

statement: The province should give first-time homebuyers direct subsidies to help them enter the market.
notes: Broad political appeal; the split is whether demand-side help or pure supply is the fix. CentreBC and NDP favour; Greens prefer supply and warn subsidies raise prices.

statement: Supportive and social housing should be expanded even in neighbourhoods that object.
notes: A NIMBY test. NDP/Greens/BCE supportive; Conservatives/OneBC emphasise neighbourhood consultation first.

statement: BC should expand private, for-profit clinics to reduce health-care wait times.
notes: The sharpest health divide. Conservatives/OneBC favour for-profit expansion; NDP, CentreBC and Greens defend public single-payer.

statement: The province should speed up hiring of foreign-trained and American health-care workers.
notes: NDP's flagship response (recruitment campaign tripled to $15M). Broadly popular, but Conservatives question cost and credential standards.

statement: Public drug coverage (pharmacare) should be expanded to cover more medicines for everyone.
notes: NDP/Greens pro; fiscal conservatives wary of the cost. Tests scope of the public system.

statement: The province should fund more supervised consumption sites and safer-supply programs.
notes: NDP/Greens support harm reduction; Conservatives/OneBC oppose and prefer treatment-first. High-salience values line.

statement: Health care in BC should remain entirely public and single-payer, with no private payment for medically necessary care.
notes: Values anchor and the purest version of the private-care fight. NDP/CentreBC/Greens affirm; Conservatives/OneBC weaken the commitment.

statement: Dental care should be added to the public health system and paid for by the province.
notes: NDP/CentreBC are expanding public dental; Conservatives prefer the private market; Greens support.

statement: Overdose-prevention sites should be expanded even where local residents and businesses object.
notes: A sharper version of q22 that forces the neighbourhood question. Conservatives/OneBC reject provincial override; Greens/NDP accept it.

statement: The province should impose minimum nurse-to-patient ratios in hospitals.
notes: NDP/CentreBC support staffing mandates; Conservatives prefer administrative flexibility and warn of cost; Greens support.

statement: BC should allow more private diagnostic imaging to cut waiting lists.
notes: A service-expansion variant of q19 that is easier to agree with. Conservatives/OneBC pro; NDP/CentreBC wary of two-tier creep.

statement: BC should approve new liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects to grow the export economy.
notes: Cross-cutting: NDP champions LNG exports; Greens strongly oppose; Conservatives/OneBC pro. Splits the NDP from its environmental base.

statement: The province should stop logging old-growth forests.
notes: Greens/BCE strong yes; NDP mixed and balancing forestry jobs; Conservatives/OneBC prioritise the resource economy.

statement: BC should require steep emissions cuts from the oil and gas sector.
notes: Greens yes; NDP balances its 2030 targets against industry; Conservatives/OneBC no. Tests the centre of the climate file.

statement: The province should invest in public transit and rail rather than expanding highways.
notes: Greens/progressives yes; Conservatives/OneBC are highway-focused. Clear spending-direction split.

statement: Industrial carbon pricing should apply to BC's largest emitters.
notes: Less polarising than the consumer carbon tax. NDP/Greens favour; Conservatives/OneBC sceptical; useful as a softer climate probe.

statement: BC should protect at least 30% of its land and water by 2030.
notes: Greens/BCE strongly support; NDP is committed; Conservatives/OneBC downplay the target against resource access.

statement: BC should require that all new cars sold by 2035 be electric.
notes: Greens yes; NDP cautious about cost and rural drivers; Conservatives/OneBC oppose a mandate. Tests climate ambition vs affordability.

statement: BC should fast-track approvals for mining and resource projects to create jobs.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC signature promise; NDP wants 'yes, with environmental rules'; Greens oppose. Clean extractive-economy axis.

statement: BC should end public subsidies to the fossil fuel industry.
notes: Greens/BCE yes; NDP mixed; Conservatives/OneBC no. Targets where the money goes rather than consumer costs.

statement: BC should fully implement the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA).
notes: The defining flashpoint of the 2026 campaign. NDP/CentreBC/Greens affirm; Conservatives call repeal a top priority; OneBC is critical. Even though only ~6-13% rank it a top issue, it is a strong values differentiator.

statement: DRIPA should be amended to make clear that Indigenous nations do not have veto power over resource projects.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC framing; Eby has floated amendments to the NDP's own law; splits the NDP base. Pairs with q37 to map the whole debate.

statement: The province should share resource revenue with First Nations whose territories host the projects.
notes: NDP/Greens/BCE support revenue sharing; Conservatives wary of the precedent; tested by pipeline and LNG benefit agreements.

statement: Aboriginal title and rights should be affirmed in provincial law.
notes: Greens/BCE strong yes; NDP supportive but cautious; Conservatives/OneBC oppose statutory affirmation. Rights-anchor version of q37.

statement: BC should fund Indigenous-led child and family services.
notes: Broadly supported across parties — consensus item, low differentiation. Flag for possible removal at the freeze gate.

statement: First Nations should have a decisive role in land-use decisions on their traditional territories.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC call this a 'veto'; NDP/CentreBC/Greens accept consent-based decision-making. The consent-vs-consult distinction is the real divide.

statement: The province should prioritise Indigenous-owned businesses in public procurement.
notes: NDP/BCE pro as economic reconciliation; Conservatives question preferential treatment; CentreBC split. Lower salience than q37-q42.

statement: Treaty negotiations should be accelerated even if they cost the province money and create uncertainty for industry.
notes: NDP/Greens/BCE pro; Conservatives prioritise certainty for resource developers. Trades reconciliation against investment climate.

statement: BC should expand funding for Indigenous languages and cultural programs.
notes: Broadly supported across the spectrum — consensus item, low differentiation. Flag for possible removal at the freeze gate.

statement: Public drug use should be illegal and the decriminalization pilot should not be revived.
notes: Eby already ended the pilot; Conservatives/OneBC want the ban permanent; Greens/BCE object on health grounds. Post-hoc but sharply differentiating.

statement: Bail should be made tougher for repeat violent offenders.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC centre street-crime and bail reform; NDP has moved toward it; Greens/BCE worry about Charter rights and jailing the un-convicted.

statement: The province should expand involuntary care for people with severe addiction and mental illness.
notes: NDP has expanded it (and would go further); Conservatives/OneBC want more; Greens/BCE raise civil-liberties concerns. Cuts across left-right.

statement: Funding for police should be increased to address street disorder.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC yes; Greens/BCE prefer prevention spending; NDP mixed. Force-structure vs social-spend divide.

statement: Safer-supply programs should be scaled back in favour of treatment and recovery.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC support scaling back; NDP defends harm reduction; Greens/BCE oppose. The recovery-vs-harm-reduction axis.

statement: BC should create many more publicly funded treatment and recovery beds.
notes: Near-consensus on the goal; the split is on funding scale and how it pairs with harm reduction. NDP/CentreBC emphasise it.

statement: Municipalities should be allowed to ban public drug use in their own bylaws.
notes: Conservative/OneBC strong yes; NDP has imposed restrictions province-wide; Greens/BCE object to patchwork rules. Local-autonomy vs uniform-health-policy test.

statement: Courts should be able to order addiction treatment for repeat offenders.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC pro; NDP cautiously open; Greens/BCE opposed. Tougher cousin of q48.

statement: BC should invest more in youth prevention and after-school programs to reduce future crime.
notes: Broadly supported across parties — consensus item, low differentiation. Flag for possible removal at the freeze gate.
